healthcareSystem: Limited public healthcare. Hospital Nacional Guido Valadares in Dili is the main facility. District hospitals exist but are very basic. Some private clinics in Dili offer better care. Serious conditions require evacuation to Darwin (Australia), Bali, or Singapore.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is poor. The national hospital in Dili is the best facility but still lacks modern equipment and specialists. Portuguese and Tetum are official languages — English is spoken by some medical staff in Dili. Outside Dili, healthcare is extremely basic.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Dili open 8am-6pm weekdays, 8am-1pm Saturday. Very few pharmacies outside the capital.
pharmacyTips: Limited pharmacy options, mostly in Dili. Stock is unreliable and medications may not meet international quality standards. Bring all essential medications from home. Portuguese, Tetum, and some English spoken.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is minimal. Availability is the main challenge. Bring all needed medications with documentation in Portuguese or English.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications in English or Portuguese. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring generous extra supplies for travel outside Dili.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation is essential. Evacuation to Darwin or Bali costs $20,000-80,000. Ensure coverage includes malaria treatment and remote area travel.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Malaria is present in many areas, especially rural and border regions — prophylaxis is strongly recommended. Dengue fever is common.

waterNotes: Tap water is not safe to drink anywhere in Timor-Leste. Use bottled water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice unless made from purified water. Boil or treat water if bottled water is unavailable. Hotels in Dili generally provide safe water.
foodSafetyTips: Eat thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid raw salads and unpeeled fruits. Seafood and rice dishes from reputable restaurants in Dili are generally safe. Be extra cautious with street food. Fish and grilled meats from established restaurants are safer options.
medicalTourismNote: Timor-Leste is not a medical tourism destination. Patients needing specialist care are evacuated to Darwin (Australia), Bali/Jakarta (Indonesia), or Singapore.
metaDescription: Health guide for Timor-Leste: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, malaria info, water safety, and medical evacuation advice.

hospitals.name: Hospital Nacional Guido Valadares
hospitals.notes: Main national hospital. Emergency department. Basic facilities. Portuguese, Tetum, and some English spoken. Best option in the country but still limited.

hospitals.name: Stamford Medical Clinic
hospitals.notes: Private clinic popular with expats and international workers. Better standard of care for routine issues. English spoken.

hospitals.name: Timor-Leste General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. A few dental clinics in Dili.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is basic. A small number of private dental clinics operate in Dili. Equipment is often outdated.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, private clinics in Dili are the best option. Complex dental work requires evacuation to Darwin or Bali.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. Some NGOs provide counseling services.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited. Pradet (local NGO) provides some counseling. Consider telehealth services from your home country.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Timor-Leste.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads outside Dili are rough and unpaved.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility needs should plan carefully. Most buildings lack ramps or elevators. Arrange private transport and assistance in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing at major hospitals in Dili.
covidStatus.notes: COVID treatment capacity is limited. Serious respiratory illness may require evacuation.

insuranceClaimProcess: Obtain itemized receipts from providers. Cash payment is expected at most facilities. Private clinics may accept credit cards. Save all documentation for insurance reimbursement. Contact your insurer's assistance line before evacuation.

commonCosts.note: Timor-Leste uses the US dollar. Costs are low but reflect basic care quality. Private clinics charge more but offer better service.

medicalEvacuation.note: Evacuation to Darwin (1-hour flight) is the fastest option. Bali and Singapore are alternatives. Ensure insurance covers air ambulance from remote areas.
